text:
If you're wrapping up anything outdoors tonight, don't dawdle, the lull we've had is closing out fast. Showers and thunderstorms move in through the evening and stick around overnight, with a soggy 80 percent chance and a quarter to half inch of rain possible, so cover what needs covering before bed. The lake's already got a Lake Wind Advisory going, south winds 15 to 25 knots kicking up 2 to 3 foot waves this evening before easing overnight, so if you're still out there, head in now rather than later.

Monday keeps the unsettled pattern going, mostly cloudy with a high near 80 that actually slides back down to the mid 70s in the afternoon behind a front. Rain looks likely most of the day, heaviest in the morning into early afternoon, and the forecasters are flagging a strong thunderstorm as possible late morning into early afternoon too, so if you've got flexibility, push outdoor plans to the evening when things trend calmer and drier. The models agree it's a wet day, they just don't agree on exactly how wet, so keep the rain jacket handy regardless.
